analysis: All four changed files are test-only (ModelCalibrationTests.swift, ProductionModelCalibrationTests.swift, KVPoolSweepWiringTests.swift, IdleCalibrationCoordinatorTests.swift). They add no production code, no network, auth, attestation or crypto surface, no key handling and no new file I/O. The tests exercise calibration and shape-warmup lifecycle behavior: prompt sizing, warmup precedes calibration, foreground preemption, cancellation provenance, and the proactive KV sweep deferring while an idle calibration session is active. The calibration prompts are synthetic fixtures (ModelCalibrationTokenizer), not consumer data, so A-001 is not exposed by the tests. They assert that warmup and calibration add no billing or generation counters ([0,0,0,0]) and that the service budget returns to 0, which is availability and accounting hygiene. The test-only extensions use @testable internals (modelCalibration.shapeWarmupModeOverride, shapeWarmupCellsCompleted) and sit in the test target, so they do not widen production attack surface. The PR's production-side changes are not in the supplied units: ModelCalibrationPolicy shape-warmup, the IdleCalibrationCoordinator cancellationSource, the sweep gating in GlobalKVCacheBudget.proactiveReclaimSweep, and the EngineV2Bridge startShapeWarmupIfNeeded/runShapeWarmupBeforeServing paths. I cannot verify that they preserve foreground preemption (T-010, T-029) or that warmup stays out of the served and billed rate/telemetry that feeds coordinator routing. No finding is supported by the supplied evidence. If source from that production batch exists, integration should confirm that warmup and probe work is excluded from rate evidence, that the startup warmup is bounded and cancellable before serving, and that deferring the sweep behind an idle session cannot starve memory reclamation indefinitely (the T-029 availability aspect).
